# Which conformance fixtures leak, and by how much.
#
# One row per runnable fixture: its name, then the number of allocations
# that never got a matching free on the path the fixture takes, measured
# with FERN_RC_TRACE and paired by pointer. 0 is clean.
#
# Generated by TestConformanceLeakCensusX86_64; regenerate with
# FERN_LEAK_CENSUS_DUMP=1. Negative fixtures (an expected*error file) are
# not listed — they are not supposed to compile.
#
# THIS FILE IS A GAP LIST, NOT A SPECIFICATION. Every non-zero row is a
# leak the compiler has today and should not have. The pin exists so a
# fixture cannot start leaking, or leak more, without the change that did
# it being visible; a row going DOWN is progress and also fails, so the
# improvement gets recorded rather than absorbed.
#
# Measured 2026-09-03: 471 fixtures, 391 clean, 80 leaking, 8626
# unpaired allocations. The distribution is heavily skewed — the median
# leaking fixture is 2, and regex_captures_assert alone is 5987 of the
# total.
#
# The counts are pinned; the alloc SITES are not. A site is a runtime
# return address, so it moves with any codegen change and would churn
# this file for reasons unrelated to reference counting. Sites are
# printed on failure instead, where addr2line on a -g build turns one
# into a source line.
